text: The 19-service target keeps one DEV sandbox database per service release: rwb_sandbox for rwb-source-data, built in rwb_sandbox_next and renamed after the verifier passes. The generator is tools/sandbox-generator in package th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.sourcedata.sandbox, a separate build module of the rwb-source-data repository that is never packaged into the service artefact, and the sandbox database holds three schemas only: public as the ACE test double, recovery for the 30 read-only views and rwb_source_data for this service's tables and the four extension tables.
why: Legacy RWB-E1-065 gives one sandbox database, one pipeline stage and one generator package for the monolith and says nothing about the 19-service target, and Architecture v5 gives the one ACE server with 19 service schemas and no sandbox at all, so the count and the packaging boundary had to be read.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-065 sections 3, 4 and 13; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 8, 9, 15, 29 and 41; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-01, DP-02, DP-05 and DP-15; Ownership Map v1
confirm: Solution architect and the platform DB owner at the wave 1 entry check
impact: The story can be built and tested as written. If a shared sandbox is chosen instead, the three-schema rule and the read-only role of the app and DB stories change, and DP-01 and DP-02 have to be re-read for the sandbox.

text: The contract of the sandbox build is read as the pipeline stage interface and its input and output profile: the stage contract of 12.6 with trigger, inputs, outputs, publication, idempotency key, restart behaviour and failure checks; the seed profile schema as data with every value an override; the database and role contract with three schemas and the read-only role rwb_sandbox_read; the failure contract with the four legacy checks and the fail-closed rule; the four fixtures; and the nine contract tables of section 12.
why: No source in the set describes a contract for a build tool or a pipeline stage: Architecture v5 fixes contracts for REST, events, Temporal, files and SQL views only, and the legacy story described its stage inside the story body.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-065 sections 12 and 13; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 11 (five call types); Template and Rules v1 R7.2 s12 and R5.5 DP-15
confirm: Tech lead of rwb-source-data and the solution architect at the baseline review
impact: The six contract criteria and their six test cases can be written and tested as they stand. If a platform-wide build-tool contract standard is issued later, the document is re-tagged as a new baseline and the four fixtures follow it.

text: The sandbox database scope and role are read as one DEV database per service release with one read-only role: rwb_sandbox with the build database rwb_sandbox_next, schemas public, recovery and rwb_source_data, and the role rwb_sandbox_read holding USAGE and SELECT on schema recovery and schema rwb_source_data, no privilege on schema public, no INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE or TRUNCATE anywhere, mapped to the DEV group RWB-DEV-RW-TRIBE, with the credential held by the platform DB owner.
why: Legacy RWB-E1-065 names the role and the database for the monolith only, and Architecture v5 names the 19 service logins and no sandbox role, so the role name and the database scope of the target are a reading and not a quotation.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-065 sections 3, 4 and 13; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 8, 11 and 29; Ownership Map v1
confirm: ACE DBA and the platform DB owner before the first non-DEV use
impact: The build, the grants and the checks can be written and tested as they stand. If the role is renamed, the grant block, the checks and the two refusals change together and the database story is re-issued.
